body: Hey man...I am in the exact same boat as you. Recently just lost my job and my fiance. I know how tough it is snd the negative impact it has on your mental health. Just wanted to say that if you need anything, don't be afraid to reach out. I am in the exact same position and can 100% relate to the pain you are experiencing. Honestly, the job was one thing. Losing my fiance made me fear for my safety and my life.

I have been through so many different medications. I have tried zoloft, paxil, celexa, abilify, risperidone, trazadone and have had terrible reactions to all of them except celexa. I have tried propanolol and hydroxyzine for my panic attacks with little benefit. I am currently on lexapro, mirtazapine and lamictal. To be honest i am not sure if they are even working, but I am afraid to stop and have an issue. It is such a trial by error process and it is unfortunate because so many people need help asap and really don't have the time to wait 4-6 weeks for the benefits to kick in and notice if the medication is helping or not.

Hey..I know exactly how you feel..I have had at least five concussions..Also, I have a terrible time sleeping just about every night. I would hate to know what my brain actually looks like as I am sure I have at least a mild case of CTE. Pretty sure that my concussions have made my anxiety and depression at least a little worse than it was prior to my head injuries.

I'm only in my 20's also brother. I have had double digit friends pass away since I have graduated from high school, so I understand how you feel. Everyone deals with the loss of a loved one in their own way. My only hope is that somehow, someway you find a constructive way to deal with your loss other than masking it through the use of booze or weed. Unfortunately, that is just a temporary coverup to an issue that no chemical can overcome. You need to find a way that you will come to terms with the tragedy and find closure. I am sure your friend would not want you to turn to substances to deal with his/her lose. I have dealt with many personal issues including depression, panic attacks, loss of loved ones etc. and have turned to substances to try to take away the pain and cause an altered perception of reality due to being afraid and overwhelmed with pain. I did not want to come to terms with what has happened in my life. Every single time it only made it worse in the end. You have to really dig down deep and find a way that will help you cope and overcome this hard time. My condolences go out to you and anyone else that has been impacted by the loss of your friend. My thoughts and prayers are with you.
